title: Quantify uncertainty and design sensitivity in the scan-disjoint matrisome benchmark
question: How much support do the released array rankings give for transfer, and how much do phase weighting, array omissions and scanner-day comparisons change that interpretation?
scope: Retrospective analysis of the existing three target-cohort summaries and Rome scanner margins. The benchmark rankings, phase counts and scan-order imbalance are already public. No participant-level inputs, training or source downloads.
steps: Pin the two aggregate inputs and check case, comparator, pair and tie counts.
Enumerate rank-sum null distributions under array-label exchangeability, preserving U.S. phase margins. Report nominal and three-target Holm results.
Reweight and omit U.S. phases, bound the impact of individual array omissions, and identify all attainable Rome within-day ranking totals from its scanner margins.
deliverables: Reproducible offline calculation with synthetic exhaustive checks
Machine-readable results and a source-linked research note
acceptance: Distinguish exact arithmetic from the assumptions about arrays and scanner order needed for inference.
Use the scan-disjoint fit for all tests and keep sensitivity analyses outside the three-target test family.
Distinguish sharp bounds compatible with aggregates from observed deletion or scanner-adjusted results.
